specimens.name: Opal
specimens.note: Fluoresces in brilliant blues and greens under UV. Amorphous SiO₂ with variable water content.

specimens.name: Scapolite
specimens.note: Strongly fluoresces yellow under UV. Part of the scapolite group of aluminosilicate minerals.

specimens.name: Franklinite with Calcite and Willemite
specimens.note: Zinc ore mineral that doesn't fluoresce, but associated willemite (green under UV) and calcite (pinkish under UV) do.

specimens.name: Sodalite (Hackmanite variety)
specimens.note: Named for its sodium content. This hackmanite variety fluoresces orange under long wavelength UV light.

specimens.name: Adamite
specimens.note: Zinc arsenate hydroxide mineral that fluoresces yellow-green under UV. Eye-catching crystals make it a collector favorite.

specimens.name: Sphalerite
specimens.locality: Junction Shaft, Bisbee, Cochise Co., Arizona
specimens.note: Most common zinc ore. Fluoresces brilliant yellow-orange under UV. Also triboluminescent—generates light when mechanically stressed.

specimens.name: Scapolite
specimens.note: Part of the scapolite group of aluminosilicate minerals. Strongly fluoresces yellow under UV.

specimens.name: Fluorite
specimens.note: The phenomenon of 'fluorescence' derives its name from this mineral. Green in natural light, fluoresces blue under UV.

specimens.name: Willemite
specimens.note: Zinc silicate found with franklinite. Unassuming in natural light but fluoresces bright green under UV.

specimens.name: Willemite with Calcite
specimens.note: Willemite (fluorescing green under UV) surrounded by calcite (fluorescing pink-purple under UV).

specimens.name: Calcite
specimens.note: Most common mineral to show fluorescence under UV. Shows large range of fluorescent colors. This sample fluoresces vibrant pink.

specimens.name: Scapolite
specimens.note: Part of the scapolite group of aluminosilicate minerals. Strongly fluoresces yellow under UV.

specimens.name: Tantalite
specimens.note: Tantalum oxide mineral. Primary ore of tantalum, used in surgical steel alloys, glass refraction, and electronics capacitors. Donated February 1968 by Donald C. Swanson.

specimens.name: Columbite
specimens.locality: Ingersoll mine, Keystone, South Dakota, USA
specimens.note: Niobium oxide mineral from pegmatite. Niobium used in jet engines, rockets, and superconductors. Purchased September 1969 from Filer's.

specimens.name: Eudialyte
specimens.locality: Sheffield Lake, Kipawa Lake Area, Quebec, Canada
specimens.note: Rare cyclosilicate, minor ore of zirconium. Contains uranium and lead making it useful as a geochronometer. Donated November 1969 by Chas. Blackburn.

specimens.name: Niocalite
specimens.note: Rare niobium sorosilicate mineral first described by Dr. E.H. Nickel in drill core from the Oka carbonatite. Donated January 1971 by Jacques Grenier.

specimens.name: Pyrochlore
specimens.locality: Open Pit, St. Lawrence Columbium and Metal Corp., Oka, Quebec, Canada
specimens.note: Complex oxide containing niobium. Principal ore of niobium. Donated May 6, 1971 by Dr. G. Gordon Suffel.

specimens.name: Wolframite
specimens.locality: Panasqueira Mine, Castelo Branco District, Centro Region, Portugal
specimens.note: Iron-manganese tungstate, important tungsten ore. Tungsten has highest melting point of any element (3422°C). Donated 2006 by Arnim Walter.

specimens.name: Pollucite
specimens.locality: Tanco Mine, Bernic Lake, English River District, Manitoba, Canada
specimens.note: Cesium-rich zeolite from lithium pegmatites. 82% of world's pollucite reserves are at Tanco mine. Donated December 13, 1968 by Dr. R.W. Hutchinson.

specimens.name: Lepidolite
specimens.locality: Tanco Mine, Bernic Lake, English River District, Manitoba, Canada
specimens.note: Phyllosilicate from lithium-bearing pegmatites. Secondary ore of lithium and major source of rubidium. Donated December 1956 or January 1957 by Dr. R.W. Hutchinson.

specimens.name: Spodumene
specimens.locality: Noumas Mine, Cape Province, South Africa
specimens.note: Lithium-bearing pyroxene, principal ore of lithium in hard rock deposits. About half of lithium production is from spodumene. Donated April 4, 1974 by Dr. R.W. Hutchinson.

specimens.name: Cesium-rich Beryl
specimens.locality: Beryl Pit, Tanco Mine, Bernic Lake, English River District, Manitoba, Canada
specimens.note: Very rare form of the cyclosilicate mineral beryl. Beryl group includes gems like emerald and aquamarine. Collected ~1999, donated 2023 by Dr. R.L. Linnen.

specimens.name: MQM Alteration (Mica-Quartz after Microcline)
specimens.locality: Tanco Mine, Bernic Lake, English River District, Manitoba, Canada
specimens.note: Distinct alteration style known to host high grade tantalum mineralization at Tanco mine. With columbite-tantalite. Collected ~1999, donated 2023 by Dr. R.L. Linnen.

specimens.name: Columbite-tantalite mineralization
specimens.locality: Tanco Mine, Bernic Lake, English River District, Manitoba, Canada
specimens.note: Very coarse grained col-tan mineralization rich in niobium and tantalum. No col-tan mining currently in Canada due to regulations. Collected ~1999, donated 2023 by Dr. R.L. Linnen.

specimens.name: Dendritic Columbite
specimens.locality: 511 Zone, Tanco Mine, Bernic Lake, English River District, Manitoba, Canada
specimens.note: Dark brown to black niobium oxide with dendritic crystal growth in hematitic alteration of feldspar. Dendritic forms indicate rapid crystallization. Collected ~1999, donated 2023 by Dr. R.L. Linnen.

specimens.name: Wulfenite
specimens.note: Lead molybdate mineral, typically bright orange-red to yellow-orange. From Al Kington Collection, donated by Nancie Irving.

specimens.name: Sodalite
specimens.locality: Princess Sodalite Quarry, Bancroft, Ontario, Canada
specimens.note: Blue mineral named for sodium content, formed in nepheline syenites and related rocks. From Al Kington Collection, donated by Nancie Irving.

specimens.name: Gypsum (Fishtail Selenite variety)
specimens.note: Soft sulfate mineral. 'Fishtail selenite' is twinned gypsum crystal resembling a fish's tail. Primary component of drywall. From Al Kington Collection.

specimens.name: Rhodochrosite
specimens.note: Manganese carbonate, typically rose-red. Veins resemble strips of bacon—nicknamed 'Bacon Rocks' by UWO students. From Al Kington Collection.

specimens.name: Gypsum (Gypsum Rose variety)
specimens.note: Rose-like formation of gypsum crystals with abundant sand grains. Primary component of drywall/Gyprock. From Al Kington Collection.

specimens.name: Variscite
specimens.locality: Clay Canyon, near Fairfield, Utah County, Utah, USA
specimens.note: Rare hydrated aluminum phosphate forming nodules. Green color from chromium in crystal structure. From Al Kington Collection.

specimens.name: Rosasite
specimens.note: Carbonate mineral forming balls or coatings on rocks, often associated with red limonite and other colorful minerals. From Al Kington Collection.

specimens.name: Rugose Corals, Brachiopods, and Bryozoans
specimens.note: Plate of multiple fossil species. Filter feeders from Middle Ordovician to Late Permian seas. Donated by Duncan Robertson, collected on 1984 Petro-Canada Field Trip led by Dr. Gordon E. Tebbut.

specimens.name: Massive Argillite
specimens.locality: Greens Creek Mine, Admiralty Island, Alaska, USA
specimens.note: From largest silver mine in the US. Dolomitic argillite from base of Hyd group with quartz-carbonate ladder veining. Carnian-Norian age (~220Ma). Donated by Hecla Mining per Dr. Dean McDonald.

specimens.name: Massive Fine Base Metal (MFB) Mineralization
specimens.locality: Greens Creek Mine, Admiralty Island, Alaska, USA
specimens.note: Ore with >50% sulfide—sphalerite, galena, tetrahedrite dominating over pyrite. From largest silver mine in the US. Donated by Hecla Mining per Dr. Dean McDonald.

specimens.name: White Carbonate-Rich (WCA) Mineralization
specimens.locality: Greens Creek Mine, Admiralty Island, Alaska, USA
specimens.note: Ore with <50% sulfide, dominated by carbonate gangue. Contains pyrite, sphalerite, galena, tetrahedrite, chalcopyrite. Donated by Hecla Mining per Dr. Dean McDonald.

specimens.name: Silver Ore
specimens.note: From longest continuously operating mine in Cobalt area (1905-1967). ~2 foot silver vein section with calcite and native silver, plus leaf silver chunk. Secured by Dr. J.W. Russel ~1924.

specimens.name: Gold
specimens.note: Malleable metal occurring as nuggets or grains. Labelled as 'Dad's favourite rocks.' Donated by Dr. Richard W. Hutchinson's family.

specimens.name: Calcite and Copper
specimens.locality: Copper Corp Mine, Algoma District, Ontario, Canada
specimens.note: Calcite crystals (1-2cm) covering specimen, with druzy quartz and small copper blebs. Donated by Dr. Richard W. Hutchinson's family.

specimens.name: San Sebastian Hugh Zone Sample
specimens.note: Polymetallic sample from Hugh Zone of Francine Vein. Au 0.17 ppm, Ag 824.00 ppm. From high-grade silver producer in Mexican Silver Belt. Donated by Hecla Mining per Dr. Dean McDonald.

specimens.name: Diatreme
specimens.note: From a diatreme (volcanic pipe from gaseous eruption). Gneiss rafts are 3.2 billion years old and co-extensive with gold mineralization. Donated by Dr. Norm A. Duke.

equipment.name: Sprengnether Horizontal Component Seismometer
equipment.note: Series H seismometer designed in the 1940s. Uses horizontal pendulum and electromagnetic field to measure side-to-side seismic movements (N-S or E-W). Originally designed for tracking hurricanes.

equipment.name: Willmore Seismograph
equipment.note: Designed by Patrick Willmore in early-mid 1950s. Horizontal component seismometer using a damped mirror to reflect light onto photosensitive paper. Designed as portable alternative to bulky observatory instruments.

ammonoids.name: Ammonoid Models and Fossils
ammonoids.note: Reconstructed ammonoids from the Bearpaw Formation (Late Cretaceous). Extinct relatives of squids, octopuses, cuttlefish and Nautilus. Some specimens show mosasaur bite marks—crater-like punctures matching mosasaur tooth patterns. Display created by Dr. Cam Tsujita.
